markets_intro: HPLEx (High-Power Light/Plasma Excimer) technology addresses disinfection and treatment steps in water-handling markets. Because the disclosure materials describe the technology but not yet a shipping product, market relevance below is expressed as application families with named buyer types, not as committed sales channels. Application families: municipal drinking water; municipal wastewater and reuse; industrial process water (food-and-beverage, pharmaceutical ultrapure pre-treatment); aquaculture and horticulture irrigation; point-of-entry/point-of-use commercial buildings. Each family lists the decision-maker who buys, the trigger event that starts procurement, and what must be true for HPLEx to enter consideration.
market_size_intro: Figures below are reported strictly at their published definition boundary. The three commonly quoted 'UV water' figures — (a) UV disinfection equipment, (b) ultraviolet water treatment systems including consumer units, and (c) advanced-oxidation processes — overlap but are not interchangeable; this report never adds them together and never substitutes one for another. Figures confirmed only through publisher summaries carry the summary-verified grade.
customers: Municipal segment buyers are utility engineering departments procuring through consulting engineers (A/E firms) who write specifications; the specifying engineer is the true gatekeeper. Industrial segment buyers are plant engineering and quality/safety leads, typically reached via integrators and service programs. Consumer/commercial building segment is channel-driven (wholesale plumbing distribution), which requires a productized unit that does not yet exist for HPLEx. For each segment the table notes: buyer, influencer, procurement trigger, validation requirement.
barriers: Adoption barriers stated without patent analysis: (1) Validation pathway cost and duration — municipal UV products require dose-validation per recognized protocols before specification; (2) Incumbent installed base and service economics favoring mercury-lamp incumbents until lamp-replacement cycles open; (3) Procurement conservatism where failure of disinfection carries public-health consequences; (4) Unverified HPLEx-specific items: field durability, lamp lifetime under duty cycling, reactor-scale energy-per-log-removal versus incumbent UV — all inventor claims pending independent measurement; (5) Regulatory classification path differs by jurisdiction and application (drinking-water contact versus wastewater); (6) Supply-chain readiness for excimer sources at power levels beyond laboratory practice.
next_steps: Recommended sequence (market-only): 1. Independent performance characterization against incumbent UV on energy-per-log-removal and lamp lifetime, at an accredited third-party lab. 2. Select one beachhead segment with fastest validation path (industrial process water precedes municipal drinking water). 3. Approach two identified partners from the Potential Partners table with a non-confidential teaser before any NDA, after IP counsel consultation on disclosure strategy. 4. Apply for one tailored-collaboration study with a utility research consortium to generate citable third-party data. 5. Book exhibition space at the nearest verified trade show in the Trade Shows table to run customer-discovery interviews. No patentability or clearance conclusions are offered here; consult qualified IP counsel regarding protection and disclosure strategy before public disclosure.
